_doc: Device profiles, matched top to bottom; every 'match' rule is a case-insensitive regex on a getprop-derived field (manufacturer, model, device, soc, platform). paper_column names the paper's Table 9 column to compare against (null = not in the paper); proxy_column is the closest paper phone for a phone that is not in it (compared and labelled as a proxy; the Galaxy S23's SM8550 is one generation older than the Xiaomi 14's SM8650). max_temp_c is the cool-down gate (paper: below 28 C). energy_method is the headline method (null = decided by energy_probe.py / auto: powercap if readable, else the best battery method).

profiles.label: Galaxy S23
profiles._gate_note: over wireless adb the screen stays on, and the idle phone rests at 29.9-31.2 C battery (2026-10-06/07), above the paper's 28 C; the gate therefore also passes once the battery has stopped cooling (<= 0.2 C drop over 300 s, at most 32.5 C), i.e. the previous run's heat is gone. Each run's start temperature is recorded.

profiles.label: OnePlus 8 Pro
profiles._note: Snapdragon 865 (SM8250), 1+3+4 cores, dotprod and fp16 but no i8mm: llama.cpp must be built with -march=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16, not the default armv8.7a. The paper's oldest phone (Xiaomi 14, SM8650) is four SoC generations newer, so it is only a loose proxy.

profiles.label: Redmi 9A
profiles._note: Helio G25 (MT6762), 8x Cortex-A53, 32-bit Android 11 (armeabi-v7a only), 3.9 GB RAM, no OpenCL: CPU only (--backends cpu). Needs armeabi-v7a llama.cpp and MNN builds (the harness builds arm64-v8a only; use a wrapper that swaps the ABI). Nothing in the paper is comparable, so there is no proxy column.
